handoff: QA of B1–B35 through the dev CLI in throwaway repos: B2–B35 pass. B1 fails on its delivery, not its behaviour: no day file is opened and the 2 GB footprint is 0.91x of an empty trace, but the B1 test (trace-free-views.test.ts:86) is flaky (2 of 10 runs; it also failed the full suite), and scripts/trace-bench.ts still spawns the removed `norn cockpit` (F2).

findings.title: The B1 test is flaky: the refreshing status --watch sometimes draws only 2 frames in 150 ms
findings.repro: for i in $(seq 10); do bun test packages/cli/test/trace-free-views.test.ts; done → 2 of 10 fail: expect(frames).toBeGreaterThan(2), Received: 2 (runCli status --watch --interval 20ms, input quitAfter(150)). It also failed in the full bun test. Expected: green on every run, since CI's test:fast runs it.
findings.detail: The behaviour holds (no day file opened, footprint 0.91x of an empty trace); only the frame-count assertion is timing-bound. Make it independent of wall time, e.g. quit after N frames instead of after 150 ms. Evidence: suite.txt, suite-rerun.txt.

findings.title: scripts/trace-bench.ts runs the removed `norn cockpit`, so it measures an unknown_command error
findings.repro: In a throwaway repo, `bun packages/cli/src/main.ts cockpit --interval 5s` → exit 2 {"code":"unknown_command"}. trace-bench.ts:168 spawns exactly that and samples the RSS of a process that has already exited, so the B1 footprint numbers it prints are meaningless. Since #106 (merged in afbf58e5), the cockpit is `norn status --watch`.
findings.detail: QA measured B1 with a copy that runs `status --watch --interval` instead (and also times `status --segment`): B1-B2-B10-bench.json. The header comment (line 2, `norn cockpit`, `norn status`) needs the new names too.

criteria.repro: bun test packages/cli/test/trace-free-views.test.ts, 10 runs alone: 2 fail at trace-free-views.test.ts:86 `expect(frames).toBeGreaterThan(2)`, Received 2 (it also failed in the full `bun test`). The behaviour itself holds: status --watch refreshed 4 times with every day file chmod 000 and no error, and over a 2.15 GB / 14-day trace with 420 hooks it peaked at 156 MB against 172 MB over an empty trace (0.91x). The test that pins B1 is flaky, and scripts/trace-bench.ts, the B1 benchmark, still runs the removed `norn cockpit` (unknown_command since the #106 merge).
